mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as higher rates compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates and reducing corporate borrowing capacity.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% indicates a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a monetary policy tightening cycle that reduces corporate earnings growth and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (CPIAUCSL * FEDFUNDS) has a Rank IC below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the negative return prediction fails in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are above their 50th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by high housing starts above 1500 thousand units), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to elevated inflation risks and the likelihood of monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500, or the average return in the late-cycle expansion regime is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) indicates a contraction in the real economy, reducing corporate earnings and investor confidence, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The current level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as a strong labor market sustains consumer spending and corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 60-day forward returns, as strong consumer spending drives corporate revenue growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between RSAFS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces corporate borrowing, resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
